title: How do I report a translation issue?

posts.h:
Please use the following way to report translation errors/display errors.

Screenshot(s)
The most important part of a translation error report is the screenshot (or video). Experience shows that without this, it is very hard to impossible to solve any issue. Please provide us with a screenshot of the entire game screen and do not cut out too much. With programs like Paint (included in Windows systems), you can mark specific parts of the screenshot with arrows and such. Remember, we cannot correct what we cannot find/reproduce.

Language
Of course, we will need to know which language you are talking about. We have created a forum for each language so please stick to this standard.

Description Text
In case the screenshot is not self-explanatory (which is mostly the case!), please provide a description text along with it.

Mode, Channel, Map Title (where applicable)
If you want to report translation errors which are only visible while playing, please add any of the information above which might help us to reproduce the issue.
posts.t: How do I report a translation issue?

posts.h:
A couple of issues with the English version of the pre-launcher:



"Press start button to player Brick-Force" should be "Press start button to play Brick-Force"

The quit message "Are you sure to quit?" should be "Are you sure you want to quit?" Alternatively "Are you sure you wish to quit?"

You could also could, more succinctly ask "Quit Brick-Force?".

I just noticed this, and thought I'd bring it up.
When I go onto google translate and type in "Dirk" it automatically translates from German.
The world won't end if you guys don't correct this, but I thought I should bring it up.

Though I disagree with you on changing this because google translate says it's German, I have to say I agree it should be changed to mean "Melee" in all of the languages. Dirk is very specific, and it does not at all describe the weapons it restricts you to.

However as to why it says it's German is because the etymology of the word can be traced back to German/Dutch roots. A quote from the Wikipedia page on Dirk:
The term was spelled dork or durk during the 17th century, presumably from the Dutch, Swedish and Danish dolk, via German dolch, tolch from a West Slavic tulich. The exact etymology is unclear; the sound change from -lk to -rk is rather common in Scots and Northern English loanwords from Danish... The modern spelling dirk is probably due to Samuel Johnson's 1755 Dictionary.
But as the underlined part shows the modern spelling came from Samuel Johnson's Dictionary which was an English dictionary technically making it an English word :P
